about: How OpenEMR insurance companies get their UDS insurance category (Table 4 Lines 7-12, and the Patients by ZIP Code table). The order is: the clinic's own choice in Settings, then the company's Source of Payment Typology group (the first digit of its code), then its claim type. A null category means undecided: the next step is tried, and a company still undecided is listed as a record to fix until the clinic chooses, because the UDS has no unknown-insurance line. Every null needs a note saying why. Categories: none, medicaid, chip_medicaid, medicare, other_public, other_public_chip, private.
basis: 2026 UDS Manual, Table 4 instructions. Typology group names are PHDSC Source of Payment Typology level 1. Claim types are OpenEMR's insurance_type_codes table.

paymentTypologyGroups.name: MEDICAID
paymentTypologyGroups.note: Medicaid and CHIP can't be told apart at this level. The manual says to report them as Medicaid; a CHIP plan can be set to CHIP Medicaid in Settings.

paymentTypologyGroups.name: OTHER GOVERNMENT (Federal/State/Local) (excluding Department of Corrections)
paymentTypologyGroups.note: Too varied (VA, Indian Health Service, indigent care programs). Falls through to the claim type.

paymentTypologyGroups.name: MANAGED CARE, UNSPECIFIED (to be used only if one can't distinguish public from private)
paymentTypologyGroups.note: By its own definition this group can't tell public from private plans, so it can't decide a UDS line. Falls through to the claim type.

paymentTypologyGroups.name: NO PAYMENT from an Organization/Agency/Program/Private Payer Listed
MISCELLANEOUS/OTHER
paymentTypologyGroups.note: Too varied. Falls through to the claim type.
